title: Generically stable Keisler measures
summary: Given a first-order theory $T$ (in discrete or continuous logic) and a Borel-definable global Keisler measure $μ$ in $T$, we show that the following conditions are equivalent: $(i)$ $μ$ is a frequency interpretation measure; $(ii)$ $μ$ is definable and its canonical "random extension" $r_μ$ is generically stable in the randomization theory $T^R$; $(iii)$ $μ$ is "self-averaging". This result establishes a robust notion of generic stability for Keisler measures, which resolves a long-term research objective from previous work.
